gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a plug-and-play USB car CD player shows the car the disc's tracks as WAV files on a USB storage device. So it plays only if the car's own USB media player handles .WAV (or the radio runs Android 4.4) and the port supplies 5 V at 1.5 A. Some factory systems, such as one Hyundai infotainment manual that lists only .mp3, .wma and .flac, won't play it.
standout_why: I compared against ensightauto.com, which ChatGPT got as result 12, and itechguides.com, result 13. Ensight says only that the kit 'Presents itself to your car as a standard USB audio device' and that the port must support 'audio playback — not just charging'. iTechguides says only that 'Having a USB port alone does not guarantee that the stereo can play audio files from it' and to check the manual's 'audio formats'. Neither names WAV as the format that decides it, gives the 5 V / 1.5 A power need, or describes the test with a WAV file on a USB stick. ChatGPT's answer said only 'Not all car stereos support USB CD players.' I couldn't load the NavTV PDF (certificate error), the Amazon PDF (image only) or the manuals.plus pages (403), so I could not check them.
decides: This is the go/no-go for the USB CD player route. Before buying one (such as the BOPORO ChatGPT showed for $75.59), the shopper should copy three .WAV songs to a USB stick and play them through the car's USB port. If they play and skip forward and back, a USB CD player will most likely work. If they don't play, the USB route is out. The shopper should then use the FiiO DM13 BT over Bluetooth or AUX, or replace the radio with one of the in-dash CD receivers (Pioneer DEH-S4220BT, Sony MEX-N5300BT, Kenwood KDC-BT282U). This mechanism doesn't affect those.

findings.label: Head unit requirement
findings.value: Head unit 'Running On Android 4.4 or with USB Media Player that Supports .WAV File Playback'
findings.source_title: Aerpro Plug And Play CD Player Upgrade - ADVUSBCD | Autopro
findings.note: Retailer page quoting Aerpro's product copy. aerpro.com/product/advusbcd returned 404. The unit 'Connects to compatible OEM and aftermarket head units that feature a USB media input' and is controlled 'as you would a USB media device'.

findings.label: Compatibility test before buying
findings.value: Load 3 .WAV songs on a USB stick into the factory USB port; if they play without skipping and next/previous track works, the CD player will most likely work
findings.source_title: Aerpro Plug And Play CD Player Upgrade - ADVUSBCD | Autopro
findings.note: Same page. It also says the radio may not detect the unit 'until a cd has been inserted', which 'can take 10-20 seconds'. Some cars show song names; others show only track numbers. The longest audio track it handles is 30 minutes, so it may not suit audiobooks.

findings.label: USB power requirement
findings.value: 'Will work only with USB with 5V + 1.5A power supply'; 'Vehilce USB must support .WAV file playback'
findings.note: Connects2 is the distributor. Its page also lists USB 2.0 and CD-ROM, CD-R and CD-RW discs, and says the player is powered over the USB connection.

findings.label: Factory system that would fail the WAV test
findings.value: Hyundai Gen5W infotainment (EU English manual): 'Playable file format: .mp3 / .wma / .flac' (no WAV)
findings.source_title: General Information | Hyundai infotainment owner's manual
findings.note: This is the EU manual. It also says hubs and extension cables may stop the USB device being recognized, so plug in directly.

findings.label: Factory system that would pass the WAV test
findings.value: Hyundai manual: 'Only files with .mp3/.wma/.wav extensions can be recognised by the system'; FAT12/16/32 recommended; 'USB hard disk drives may not be recognised'
findings.note: The page doesn't name the vehicle or system. With the Gen5W page above, it shows that WAV support varies even within one car brand.
